summary: Frontend-only verification of 'YouTube clean-clip mode' in VideoPlayer.jsx. Real YouTube media cannot play in this sandbox, so window.YT was stubbed via add_init_script with an instrumented fake IFrame Player (captures playerVars; records playVideo/pauseVideo/seekTo/destroy; test-driven clock + onReady/onStateChange), so the app's real logic executed. All 7 acceptance criteria PASSED: controls=0 (native scrubber hidden) + disablekb/fs/modestbranding, onReady seekTo(start)+pauseVideo (poster at clip start), yt-toggle-play play/pause toggle with icon/aria-label flip, clip-progress-track seek constrained to [start,end] with proportional fill, end enforcement (pause+seekTo(end)+Completed badge+autoadvance overlay), start lower-bound correction (seekTo(start)), and direct <video> path with NO controls attribute + native-toggle-play overlay. One real defect found: video.play() promise is not caught, producing an unhandled rejection ('The element has no supported sources.') which raises the CRA red 'Uncaught runtime errors' overlay covering the page.

ui_bugs.issue: videoRef.current.play() returns a Promise that is never caught. When the source fails/blocked (sandbox mixkit asset returns 403; in prod: autoplay policy or unsupported source) an unhandledrejection fires ('The element has no supported sources.') and CRA's dev error overlay covers the entire page. Verified via window.__rejections. Fix: videoRef.current.play()?.catch(()=>{}) and optionally surface a friendly error state.

integration_issues.flow: Resume + clip progress bar on load
integration_issues.issue: When a saved resume position exists the player is built with playerVars.start=resume (e.g. 610 for the 600-900 clip) and seeks there, but clip-progress-fill stays 0% and clip-elapsed shows '0:00' until the first poll tick after the user presses play — the bar contradicts the actual playhead. Suggest initialising clipPct from the resume value.

issues: Clip bar labels (10px #9AA096 on #FAFAF7) remain ~2.3:1 contrast — carried over from iteration 28.
Auto-advance overlay is fixed at bottom-20, visually detached from the player on 1920px desktop (functional).

action_items: Catch the rejection from videoRef.current.play() in togglePlay() (direct-video branch) so a failed/blocked source cannot trigger an unhandled rejection / CRA error overlay.
Optional: seed clipPct from the resume position so the clip bar/elapsed match the actual start frame when resuming.
critical_code_review_comments: togglePlay(): unhandled play() promise (see above) — the only functional defect found in the new player code.

Segment enforcement lives only inside the PLAYING poll; if YouTube reports BUFFERING/CUED without PLAYING the interval is cleared and the lower/upper bound is not enforced until PLAYING resumes. Acceptable today (controls hidden so users cannot seek), but note it.
seekToPct() sets clipPct optimistically before the seek confirms; if seekTo fails the bar shows a wrong position until the next poll.
VideoPlayer.jsx is 380 lines with two near-duplicate control-overlay blocks (yt/native) — extract a shared <PlayOverlay/> to satisfy DRY.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the 7 clean-clip acceptance criteria passed; 1 defect (unhandled play() rejection) found in the direct-video regression path

Clean-clip mode is fully verified; only the unhandled video.play() promise remains open. rca_of_the_issue: togglePlay() calls HTMLMediaElement.play() without handling the returned Promise. Repro: open /library/3570c056-... (direct mp4) and click native-toggle-play while the source cannot load (403 in sandbox, or autoplay-blocked in a real browser) -> window unhandledrejection 'The element has no supported sources.' and CRA's dev overlay covers the UI. Mitigation: attach .catch() and set an error state instead of failing silently.
